nodes.label: collectionGrants.ts

nodes.label: Wire Types (types.ts)

nodes.label: arcula_grant_{collectionId} Cookie
nodes.rationale: HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/api/v1, Max-Age=43200, Secure in production; a 32-byte random token whose SHA-256 hash is the only stored form, with the same twelve-hour expiry so the cookie lapses when the row does. The cookie name is its scope — each route reads only its collection's name and looks up by collection id and token hash — so the broad path does not admit one collection's grant to another's reads.

nodes.label: isPasswordProtected
nodes.rationale: On every member-audience collection document, derived from the hash's presence; a visitor's document does not carry the field at all, not even false. nodes.label: collections.passwordHash

nodes.label: clientAddress.ts (x-arcula-client-ip)
nodes.rationale: The Lambda entry writes the gateway's sourceIp into x-arcula-client-ip with set, so a client cannot choose its own address and no forwarding header is ever trusted; locally the header is absent and every attempt shares one bucket. The residual weakness is that an address is shared behind a proxy and cheap to multiply, so the throttle raises the cost of guessing without being a proof.

nodes.label: The Unlock Throttle
nodes.rationale: One row per (address, collection, window) — the pair is the key precisely so one collection's throttle cannot lock visitors out of another's through a shared address. The window is fixed at ten minutes and floored from the attempt's own time so a row names the span it counts. Ten failures spend it and the eleventh is refused unread in one atomic claim, so two racing attempts cannot both get through; a right password deletes the counter rows. The refusal states the window and never the time left, and sends no Retry-After, which would be the same countdown.

nodes.label: graphify Scope Rule

A question about git history, CI run logs, the issue tracker, external API docs or a throwaway worktree is not a codebase question and belongs to gh, the web docs or a direct read; graphify update runs from the repository root and .graphifyignore decides what it reads.

nodes.label: Arcula Splash Mark (organic ink-blot glyph)
nodes.rationale: The identity the four raster assets share: a single solid, slightly asymmetric splat with rounded organic lobes and two opposing spikes. Its irregular silhouette survives reduction to 32x32, and its solidity allows the polarity inversion used by the maskable icon.

nodes.label: Icon Polarity Inversion (dark-on-light vs light-on-dark)
nodes.rationale: The design decision that ordinary icons are a black mark on white while the maskable icon is a cream mark on charcoal: the plain icons sit quietly in light browser chrome, and the maskable one commits to a filled dark tile so a platform mask crops colour, not white.

nodes.label: PWA Icon Set (standard + maskable)
nodes.rationale: The pair a web app manifest needs: a 192px any icon for install prompts, and a 512px maskable icon for adaptive launchers. Providing both stops Android from shrink-wrapping the standard icon inside a white rounded square.

nodes.label: Apple Touch Icon (black organic splash mark on white)
nodes.norm_label: apple touch icon (black organic splash mark on white)
nodes.rationale: The iOS home-screen icon: a solid near-black irregular blob with soft rounded lobes and opposing spikes on a plain white field, with generous padding. The bare Arcula mark with no wordmark and no rounded container of its own, because iOS applies its own corner mask.

nodes.label: Favicon 32x32 (same splash mark, downscaled)
nodes.rationale: The browser-tab icon: the same black splash mark on white, scaled to 32x32 so the lobes and spikes stay legible at the smallest size. Purely the mark, no text, no border.

nodes.label: PWA Icon 192x192 (splash mark, standard mask)
nodes.rationale: The Android/PWA any icon: identical composition to the touch icon — black mark, white background, roomy margin — at 192x192, letting the platform apply its own mask.

nodes.label: PWA Maskable Icon 512x512 (inverted: cream mark on charcoal full bleed)
nodes.norm_label: pwa maskable icon 512x512 (inverted: cream mark on charcoal full bleed)
nodes.rationale: The maskable variant inverts the polarity: a cream/off-white splash mark on a full-bleed charcoal square instead of a black mark on white. The background reaches every edge so an aggressive platform mask never reveals white corners, and the mark stays inside the maskable safe zone so it survives cropping.

nodes.label: Two-Column Metadata Layout
nodes.rationale: Identity fields sit in the left column and physical/provenance fields in the right, so the eye finds the artist first and the edition provenance second; the same left/right split is reused in the grid layout for consistency.

nodes.label: Artwork Metadata Field Set
nodes.rationale: Title, Artist Name, Serie, Media, Dimensions, Editions, Date of Creation, Place of Origin — the eight fields both PDF layouts print, and the exact vocabulary Arcula's artwork record must carry for an export to be faithful.

nodes.label: Arcula PDF Template
nodes.rationale: A print-ready portfolio layout: A4-proportioned page, collection title set unobtrusively at the top-left, one large artwork photo occupying the upper two-thirds, and a quiet two-column metadata block beneath it. The image dominates and the text is set small and unemphasised, so the page reads as a gallery wall label rather than a catalogue record.

nodes.label: Artwork Page Template
nodes.rationale: One artwork per page: a single large photograph (the artwork hanging in situ, not the bare scan) fills the frame, with the collection title as the only running header. Left metadata column holds Title (italic, as the heading), Artist Name, Serie, Media; the right column holds Dimensions, Editions, Date of Creation, Place of Origin. The split separates 'what it is' from 'its physical facts'.

nodes.label: Artworks Grid Template
nodes.rationale: The list/worksheet counterpart to the artwork page: the same collection title header, then artworks in a two-column grid of six metadata blocks per page, each block separated by a short '--' rule, with no photographs. Used to print the collection's inventory of facts rather than its images.

nodes.rationale: Hand-written CSS grid, not Mantine Grid (a wrapping flexbox that cannot stagger). grid-auto-rows plus per-card grid-row-end span N from a ResizeObserver keeps sorted DOM order, unlike CSS multi-column, with no dependency. First paint uses the variant's recorded dimensions.

nodes.rationale: Ids, not records, because refetch replaces objects. Shared across views. Select all covers only the visible page so one click cannot arm an unseen delete; a successful delete clears everything.

nodes.label: Shared Sort State
nodes.rationale: Sorting stops being a Table property: one runtime {field, direction} is written by both the Table headers and the Grid select, so the two never silently disagree. Accepted cost: a header click changes a global preference.

nodes.label: Sort Whole Collection, Then Page
nodes.rationale: One page size, one page state, one sorted set, sliced after sorting; a sort change resets to page 1 while a query change resets page and selection but keeps sort.

nodes.label: Table (artwork table view)
nodes.rationale: Stays default so nothing changes until asked. Reduced to a renderer, keeping sortable headers and the header checkbox.

nodes.label: List Toolbar
nodes.rationale: One wrapping row with a left action group and a right group whose Grid-only controls disappear in Table; the stable count position stops the toolbar jumping on toggle.

nodes.label: UserSettings (versioned browser-storage object)
nodes.rationale: One versioned key so a future preference needs no new key; a total parser defaults to table/title-asc for any bad input and unavailable storage degrades to in-memory. Per browser, global across collections.

nodes.label: View Toggle (icon-only segmented control)
nodes.rationale: Dumb controlled control with group label, per-segment accessible names and tooltips; toggling makes no request and resets nothing.

nodes.label: Access Grant
nodes.rationale: A 32-byte token kept only as its SHA-256 hash, in cookie arcula_grant_{id} (Path=/api/v1, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, twelve hours). The broad path covers the media proxy; a grant admits exactly what a visitor sees.

nodes.label: Arcula
nodes.rationale: Collection management for independent collectors who own the work. Built on the assumption that art is not tidy data: the fields are the ones a collector actually has, types leave room for awkward cases (circa 1889, workshop attribution, paid vs current value, provenance as a chain), and the data model refuses to treat an unset field and an empty field as the same thing. Renamed from Custodia on 28 September 2026.

nodes.label: collection_collaborators
nodes.rationale: Membership row making an account a Collaborator: reads every live work including drafts and a deleted work by id, edits works and settings, but does not administer access.

nodes.label: Deleted View
nodes.rationale: Soft delete is a deletedAt stamp: the work disappears from live lists without its bytes moving. The Deleted view lists stamped works most-recent-first and restores one or several.

nodes.label: favicon.svg as Icon Source of Truth
nodes.norm_label: favicon.svg as icon source of truth
nodes.rationale: Every raster size generated from the single-path glyph; the maskable variant is the one to regenerate.

nodes.label: Single-use Invitation Token
nodes.rationale: The invitation mail is the only place the raw token exists; acceptance needs that link plus a signed-in account whose address matches.

nodes.label: Lock Screen
nodes.rationale: A refused collection read answers 403 password-required and folds to the Lock screen; unlock is throttled per address and collection in a fixed ten-minute window; a password change revokes every outstanding grant.

nodes.label: Mail Identity
nodes.rationale: One composition point for the four mails; normalised sender, optional Reply-To, no tracking, plain-text twin. EMAIL_PROVIDER anything other than mailpit/resend is a configuration error, not a fallback.

nodes.label: Mantine Theme as the Only Styling Source
nodes.norm_label: mantine theme as the only styling source
nodes.rationale: No global stylesheet; typography, spacing and defaults all live in theme.ts.

nodes.label: Media Proxy (GET /api/v1/media)
nodes.rationale: Nothing is served straight from object storage: the proxy re-checks visibility per request, so one authorization rule covers the row and the bytes. A photo is never more readable than its artwork; a document is member-only.

nodes.label: Ownership Transfer
nodes.rationale: Previous owner stays as a collaborator; a failed notice answers emailSent: false and never undoes the transfer.

nodes.label: Protected Collection
nodes.rationale: Protected is a second condition on a Public collection, not a third visibility state. Membership bypasses the challenge; a Private collection stays closed even to an Access grant. ADR-0005.

nodes.label: Shared Zod Validation Contract
nodes.rationale: Validation in shared schemas used by API and forms so both sides accept and reject the same input.

nodes.label: Skins (Public Collection Pages)
nodes.rationale: The public collection and single-artwork pages are a separate presentational system in apps/web/src/skins.

nodes.label: Free Tier Collection Cap
nodes.rationale: One owned collection on free; shared collections do not count.

nodes.label: URL Scheme: Readable Slug + Id
nodes.rationale: Only the id is a lookup key; the slug lives in the URL and nowhere else, so a rename cannot orphan artworks. Parsing splits on the last hyphen and ids are minted hyphen-free.

nodes.label: View Switch as Presentation-Only Change
nodes.rationale: Keeping page, selection and scroll and issuing no request is why the parent list component must own that state rather than either view.

nodes.label: The Mutation Bar for Tests
nodes.rationale: Assert external behaviour of ours, not Mantine markup or jsdom-unlayoutable arithmetic; SegmentedControl behaviour, copy, breakpoints and ResizeObserver wiring are left untested because they would test the stub.

nodes.label: The API Is the Only Way to the Data
nodes.norm_label: the api is the only way to the data
nodes.rationale: Every read and write goes through a route that resolves the session and checks membership or visibility before touching a row, which is why there is no separate security-rules layer to audit.

nodes.label: The Spreadsheet Flattening Problem
nodes.rationale: A spreadsheet promises the collection is a table: one row per work, one column per attribute. Art is not tidy data, so spreadsheets do not fail at storing it — they fail silently, letting distinctions flatten without notice. Founding motivation for Arcula's typed data model.

nodes.label: The Collection Is the Only Visitor Gate
nodes.norm_label: the collection is the only visitor gate
nodes.rationale: A visitor sees a published, live work exactly when its collection is public; a draft, a deleted work and a private collection are one answer. An artwork carries no visibility flag of its own. Decision in ADR-0003.

nodes.label: The Boundary Is Access Administration
nodes.rationale: A collaborator changes every setting (public/private included), creates, edits, imports, bulk-deletes, restores and sweeps exactly as the owner does, and may leave; the owner alone invites, resends, revokes, removes and transfers, and cannot leave without transferring. GET /collections/:id/access is member-readable but the pending offers are the owner's alone, and the tier cap counts owned collections only.

nodes.label: access.ts (access verdicts)
nodes.rationale: Pure over loaded rows: the membership fact (owner, collaborator, nobody) and the visitor rule (the collection is the only gate, with an Access grant as the second condition on a Protected one), so the verdict is testable without a DOM or a server.

nodes.label: artworkRead.ts (the single read path for Artworks)
nodes.norm_label: artworkread.ts (the single read path for artworks)
nodes.rationale: Loads the Collection and each child table once for the whole page (at most five queries, six for a collaborator's membership row), carries no Hono type so the route owns the wire code, and takes the request's grant validity as a fact. The live list's member-only search (q) is refused ahead of the visitor verdict and filters rows already read — drafts included, deleted works never.

nodes.label: authorize.ts (loads rows, asks the write question)
nodes.norm_label: authorize.ts (loads rows, asks the write question)

nodes.label: Component Tests Need an Explicit afterEach(cleanup)
nodes.norm_label: component tests need an explicit aftereach(cleanup)
nodes.rationale: Test files run per file with a jsdom docblock and the vitest configs deliberately do not set globals, so Testing Library's automatic cleanup never registers; without an explicit cleanup each render stays in the document and the next test's queries match the previous test's rows and dialogs.

nodes.label: Correctness Floor (the test exception)
nodes.rationale: A constant asserted against its own value is removed by the bar, but a correctness floor stays: getting it wrong is a silent failure rather than a changed preference.

nodes.label: deploy-verify.ts (17-step end-to-end pass)
nodes.rationale: It takes the URL, not an environment, so it runs against either by hand; it creates a throwaway verify-<ts>@example.test account per run, so it is a write against the environment. A deploy whose host does not resolve prints the DNS records and exits successfully — the first dev deploy's shape, not a failure.

nodes.label: lambda-smoke.mjs (glibc container smoke)
nodes.rationale: It smokes the built zip in a glibc container before it ships, except on a CI runner (SKIP_LAMBDA_SMOKE=1, which has no local stand-ins), where the deploy's own end-to-end pass on the deployed Lambda is the equivalent proof.

nodes.label: Local Stack (Postgres, SeaweedFS, Mailpit)
nodes.rationale: Postgres runs in a docker/colima container, SeaweedFS is the S3 stand-in on :9000, Mailpit the SMTP/UI stand-in on :1025/:8025. scripts/stack-up.sh is idempotent so the stack can be raised repeatedly.

nodes.label: Media Proxy (GET /api/v1/media?key=…)
nodes.rationale: Media never goes straight from S3: the proxy re-checks visibility per request, which is what lets one authorization layer cover both the row and the bytes.

nodes.label: Mutation Testing Is the Acceptance Bar
nodes.norm_label: mutation testing is the acceptance bar
nodes.rationale: Change the line the test claims to cover; if it stays green, the test was not covering that. A test that fails its own mutation earns its place; one that needs three separate mutations to kill is usually two tests.

nodes.label: One Lambda Behind One HTTP API (same-origin, no CORS)
nodes.norm_label: one lambda behind one http api (same-origin, no cors)
nodes.rationale: The API and the SPA ship as one Lambda behind one HTTP API, so the app is same-origin in production and there is no CORS to configure. A non-/api path returns the built index.html (deep links included) while /api/* runs the routes.

nodes.label: Request Flow: browser → API Gateway → Lambda → Postgres/S3
nodes.norm_label: request flow: browser → api gateway → lambda → postgres/s3

nodes.label: requireMemberCollection / requireMemberArtwork
nodes.rationale: The one write question — owner or collaborator — that every write path asks, so the write boundary is defined in a single place rather than re-derived per route.

nodes.label: Test Altitude Doctrine
nodes.rationale: The suite is fast, so volume is not the problem; altitude is. The question before writing a test is not 'is this worth covering?' but 'Would this fail if Mantine (or Hono, or Drizzle) changed, or only if we changed?' A test that answers the library asserts the library's behaviour, costs a reader, and buys nothing because the library tests itself.

nodes.label: Three Test Tiers
nodes.rationale: Tier 1 is pure logic over our own data (tested directly, no DOM and no server) and is where nearly everything belongs; tier 2 is our value going into a library, tested only when the failure is invisible in review or in a screenshot (a skin's type scale leaking onto /manage, a link that looks live and goes nowhere); tier 3 is everything else — don't.

nodes.label: Acquisition Date
nodes.rationale: Stored as text, never a parsed date, because the precision a real acquisition has is the owner's to state — 'circa 1889' loses nothing to a date column that cannot hold it.

nodes.label: Acquisition Price
nodes.rationale: Kept apart from the current value because the two are different facts and neither replaces the other.

nodes.label: Artwork Document
nodes.rationale: Something attached to an artwork that is a record of it rather than a picture of it — a certificate, an invoice, a condition report, or an image of one.

nodes.label: Artwork Photo
nodes.rationale: Ordered with its siblings; the first is the work's primary thumbnail wherever it appears.

nodes.label: Collection PDF
nodes.rationale: A collection's published, live artworks exported as one document — a photo page per artwork photo (up to three) and a grid for works with none, ordered by artist then title. An export of the collection, never a second presentation of it.

nodes.label: Collection Search
nodes.rationale: Answers with the live works that match: drafts are included, deleted works never are. The query lives in the page's address so a search can be linked and revisited.

nodes.label: Current Value
nodes.rationale: What the owner believes the work is worth now, distinct from the acquisition price on purpose.

nodes.label: Deleted (and the Deleted view)
nodes.rationale: The record and its media are not destroyed; the work leaves every live list and can be brought back, and the Deleted view lists them most recently deleted first where one or several are restored.

nodes.label: Draft
nodes.rationale: A draft counts as part of the collection: the owner and collaborators see it everywhere, a visitor never does whatever the collection's own visibility.

nodes.label: Provenance
nodes.rationale: Written as prose rather than stored as fields, because a chain of hands resists structured columns.

nodes.label: Published
nodes.rationale: A published work is visible to a visitor exactly when its collection is public — the collection remains the gate.

nodes.label: Slug
nodes.rationale: Cosmetic: only the id is ever looked up, so a slug may change without breaking anything.

nodes.label: Variant
nodes.rationale: One rendered size of an artwork photo or document, at the size a page actually displays it — so variants follow display geometry rather than a fixed thumbnail ladder.

nodes.label: ApiFunction (nodejs24.x arm64 Lambda serving Hono + SPA)
nodes.norm_label: apifunction (nodejs24.x arm64 lambda serving hono + spa)
nodes.rationale: 3008 MB / 300 s, WEB_DIST=/var/task/web/dist so the Hono app and the built SPA share one artifact (arcula-api.zip / arcula-api-dev.zip). NODE_ENV=production is what makes Better Auth mark the session cookie Secure.

nodes.label: ArculaStack (one class, instantiated per environment)
nodes.rationale: One stack class instantiated once per environment via the required ENV context: no VPC, no ALB, no ECS, no RDS. Postgres lives in Supabase, created out of band. Construct ids and logical ids never vary, so the dev stack's existence does not change production's template.

nodes.label: CDK Bootstrap (once, by an admin identity)
nodes.norm_label: cdk bootstrap (once, by an admin identity)
nodes.rationale: Writes the CDKToolkit stack and cdk-* roles straight at CloudFormation, SSM, S3 and ECR, while the deploy identity may only assume those roles — so it is not part of a deploy. Idempotent; the second environment needs nothing from it.

nodes.label: CDK Package Commands and Non-Workspace Status
nodes.norm_label: cdk package commands and non-workspace status
nodes.rationale: Deliberately not a workspace member and never imports application code; the stack's vitest suite asserts only the environment conditionals (stack identity, dev-only function variables, artifact, API display name) and nothing about unconditional resources. Deploys go through scripts/deploy-prod.sh or deploy-dev.sh, never a bare cdk deploy.

nodes.label: Certificate Provisioning in us-east-1
nodes.rationale: Must be in us-east-1, the one region an HTTP-API custom domain accepts; the ARN it prints goes into .env.<env> as CERT_ARN. Dev publishes only the apex although it derives a www pair, because a www host on the dev domain has nothing to alias to.

nodes.label: Stack Context Values (-c KEY=value)
nodes.rationale: ENV is required and fails synthesis rather than defaulting, so a stack is never built without knowing which environment it is. At synth absent secrets fall back to placeholders so cdk synth stays green without credentials; deploy.sh enforces their presence and the values come from the gitignored infra/cdk/.env.<env>.

nodes.label: Api — HTTP API with one greedy /{proxy+} ANY route
nodes.norm_label: api — http api with one greedy /{proxy+} any route
nodes.rationale: A single catch-all route; spa.ts splits /api/* from the SPA inside the handler, which is what keeps the deploy to one function.

nodes.label: Media S3 Bucket with 7-Day staging/ Lifecycle
nodes.norm_label: media s3 bucket with 7-day staging/ lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Private, encrypted, enforceSSL, all public access blocked. Its staging/ lifecycle rule expires staged objects after 7 days — the backstop for abandoned uploads and orphan final objects.

nodes.label: PUBLIC_URL Two-Step Deploy
nodes.rationale: The HTTP API URL exists only after the first deploy, so production deploys, reads ExecuteApiUrl and re-deploys with the real PUBLIC_URL; the Lambda is stateless so the re-deploy costs nothing. Dev knows its host up front and skips the read-back.

nodes.label: Separate Apex and www DomainName Pairs
nodes.norm_label: separate apex and www domainname pairs
nodes.rationale: An HTTP-API custom domain serves only its exact host, so www needs its own DomainName and root ApiMapping or API Gateway answers 403 before the Lambda runs. The apex keeps its original logical ids so a redeploy is an in-place update rather than a recreate.

nodes.label: Settings Access Card (invite, resend, revoke, remove, transfer, leave)
nodes.norm_label: settings access card (invite, resend, revoke, remove, transfer, leave)
nodes.rationale: Owner sees the invite form, every pending offer (expired marked, resend/revoke) and collaborators with remove and transfer; a collaborator sees the owner and collaborators and can leave. Both endings confirm and warn that the departing account's unsaved uploads are discarded; transfer warns that it is immediate and the previous owner becomes a collaborator, and the card then re-reads itself as the collaborator's view.

nodes.label: Removal, Leaving and the Narrow Staging Purge
nodes.norm_label: removal, leaving and the narrow staging purge
nodes.rationale: DELETE …/collaborators/:userId (owner removes) and DELETE …/collaborators/me (collaborator leaves) both end access immediately and both discard only the departing account's staging prefix for that collection, best effort.

nodes.label: artwork_documents Table
nodes.rationale: Deliberately no order column: documents have no sequence and no primary thumbnail, so there is nothing for an index to mean.

nodes.label: artwork_photo_variants Table (parentKind polymorphism)
nodes.rationale: One table serves photos and image documents via parentKind (photo|document). Primary key (parentId, key) means a parent has at most one object per key, which is exactly what makes promote-at-save an idempotent upsert.

nodes.label: artwork_photos Table and the Order Invariant
nodes.norm_label: artwork_photos table and the order invariant
nodes.rationale: Unique (artworkId, order): the array position is the truth, index 0 is the app-wide primary thumbnail, and the unique constraint is what makes the save's four-pass reindex safe. name is metadata only and never reaches an object path.

nodes.label: artworks Table
nodes.rationale: All descriptive fields are text so the string typed is the string stored (the design bet). userId is a mirror of the collection owner kept in step on transfer; no route authorizes on it. status published|draft and nullable deletedAt. No per-work visibility flag: a draft counts as part of its collection. Three indexes back the owner list (collectionId, deletedAt), the visitor list (collectionId, status, deletedAt) and the create-time check; the owner list lost its userId segment with sharing.

nodes.label: Auth Tables (Better Auth Core)
nodes.rationale: user, session, account, verification. user is extended with firstName, lastName, tier (default "free") and settings (jsonb). verification exists though email verification is off, so enabling it is a config flip rather than a schema change.

nodes.label: collection_access_grants Table
nodes.rationale: Holds the SHA-256 hash of a 32-byte token, never the token, so a database leak is a set of unguessable hashes rather than working grants. Index on collectionId so a password change revokes in one statement; expiry is computed from expiresAt, never stored as a status.

nodes.label: collection_collaborators Table
nodes.rationale: Primary key (collectionId, userId), index on userId for the dashboard. The owner is not duplicated here; a row is what makes an account a collaborator and is the authorization fact for everything inside the collection.

nodes.label: collection_invitations Table
nodes.rationale: Status pending|accepted|declined|revoked with unique tokenHash. At most one pending invitation per collection and email, enforced by a partial unique index on (collectionId, lower(email)) WHERE status = 'pending'. Resending rotates token, expiry and issue time on that row, which is also the cooldown clock. Raw token exists only in the mail; expiry computed from expiresAt not a status.

nodes.label: Member-Only Collection Search (?q=) Over Ten Fields
nodes.norm_label: member-only collection search (?q=) over ten fields
nodes.rationale: A present q is a member condition ahead of the visitor verdict (404 missing, 401 no session, 403 non-member including a grant holder). Both sides normalize (NFD, diacritics stripped, lowercased), the query splits on punctuation and every term must appear somewhere in the joined text of ten declared fields; terms may match different fields. Acquisition date is searched in both stored and displayed forms. Filtering runs in the API over rows the list already read, after the verdict, so only matching works load photos — no SQL pushdown, no extension, no migration; the list read stays the single seam to replace.

nodes.label: collection_unlock_attempts Table
nodes.rationale: Primary key (ip, collectionId, windowStart) plus attempts. Keyed by the pair so one collection's throttle cannot lock visitors out of another's through a shared address. Window length is route policy not schema; the unlock route is the only reader and writer.

nodes.label: collections Table
nodes.rationale: userId is the owner. deletedAt/passwordHash are nullable so the normal state is "no password". skin is read-time defaulted and never queried on, so it needs no backfill — the deliberate contrast with deletedAt. skinOptions is validated at read time against the skin's declared options (unknown key dropped, wrong type falls back) so stale data cannot corrupt a collection. Collections are never deleted.

nodes.label: Grant Cookie Scoped by Name, Not Path
nodes.norm_label: grant cookie scoped by name, not path
nodes.rationale: The cookie is Path=/api/v1 because the media proxy is a single route for every collection's bytes, so the cookie name arcula_grant_{id} rather than the path is the scope; the row is looked up by collection id plus token hash, so a grant minted elsewhere is never consulted.

nodes.label: Invitation Loop (create, resend, revoke, preview, accept)
nodes.norm_label: invitation loop (create, resend, revoke, preview, accept)
nodes.rationale: The mail is the only place the raw token exists. Resend puts a fresh token, expiry and issue time on the same row once every 60 seconds. An invalid, expired, revoked or consumed token answers not-found like an unknown one, as does an in-app decline of anything but the caller's own live offer.

nodes.label: Lock Screen Is App Chrome Reached as a State, Not an Error
nodes.norm_label: lock screen is app chrome reached as a state, not an error
nodes.rationale: The lock is about the collection, not how it is presented, and a prompt is the portaled component a skin may not use — so the screen renders outside the skin's scope. The 403 password-required folds to a locked state; on success it calls the hook's reload so collection-then-artworks runs ordinally with the grant cookie set — one path to ready. An expired grant folds back to the lock screen rather than an error page.

nodes.label: mediaNamespaceId (Fixed Media Namespace)
nodes.rationale: Fixed at creation, since object keys derive from it: a transfer changes the owner but not the namespace, so no object moves and existing URLs keep working. Shipped 0003 (nullable, backfilled from userId) then 0004 (backfill nulls written in between, set NOT NULL); the code kept the mediaNamespaceId ?? userId fallback because the Lambda deploys before the migration.

nodes.label: Media Proxy GET /api/v1/media?key=…
nodes.rationale: Parses the key back into segments and re-checks visibility against the row per request. Final photo: member, or visitor when published and live and collection public. Final document: members only, so a forgotten-to-hide UI fails closed with 403. Staged object: the uploader while still a member of the collection the entry was staged under.

nodes.label: Media Three-Step Flow: Stage, Process, Save
nodes.norm_label: media three-step flow: stage, process, save
nodes.rationale: Stage validates type and derives the extension from the declared type (never the filename). Process decodes once with Sharp, applies EXIF orientation and encodes WebP q95. Save is one transaction writing fields, copying staged objects to final keys and upserting rows; dropped entries lose rows and their final objects are deleted after commit. An S3 copy cannot roll back with rows, so a failed save may leave orphan final objects — the accepted residual the staging lifecycle and sweep clear.

nodes.label: Self-Describing Object-Key Algebra (final vs staging)
nodes.rationale: Final keys use the collection's mediaNamespaceId; staging keys use the uploader's id so one collaborator's unsaved upload is never under another's prefix and the sweep lists only the caller's. The leading staging/ prefix is deliberate: object-store lifecycle rules match literal prefixes, so one rule expires every staged object everywhere. Segments are ids and variant keys; no user filename ever reaches a path.

nodes.label: Ownership Transfer POST /collections/:id/transfer
nodes.rationale: One transaction updates the owner, mirrors the artwork rows, persists the media namespace and swaps the two membership rows. The namespace never moves so every URL keeps working. The new owner is mailed a manage-page link; a failed notice answers emailSent: false without undoing the transfer, because the transfer commits before the mail.

nodes.label: Partial PATCH /collections/:id (absent key leaves the column alone)
nodes.norm_label: partial patch /collections/:id (absent key leaves the column alone)
nodes.rationale: Every field optional so each settings tab saves only its half; a body naming nothing is a valid no-op that does not move updatedAt, so "updated" continues to mean something was. The relaxation is strictly additive so an older cached bundle sending both fields still works; the halves cannot skew because client and server ship as one Lambda.

nodes.label: Password Write Revokes Grants in the Same Transaction
nodes.norm_label: password write revokes grants in the same transaction
nodes.rationale: A string sets or overwrites the password, null removes it, absent leaves it alone. The same transaction revokes the collection's grants so changing the password closes every open cookie. The member read carries isPasswordProtected derived from the hash's presence; the hash never leaves the server.

nodes.label: RLS Enabled With No Policies, API Connects as Table Owner
nodes.norm_label: rls enabled with no policies, api connects as table owner
nodes.rationale: Every table enables RLS with zero policies and 0006_enable_rls revokes anon/authenticated grants, guarded on the roles existing. The API connects as table owner and bypasses RLS, which keeps reads and writes working; FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY must never be added or it would subject the owner to the empty policy set and blank every read. supabase_admin's default ACLs survive because default ACLs are per-grantor (accepted, #181).

nodes.label: Collection Search as Address State (?q in the URL)
nodes.norm_label: collection search as address state (?q in the url)
nodes.rationale: The URL is the source of truth so reload, bookmark or a shared address lands on the same results; the query is written debounced with replace so live typing does not fill the Back stack, and the canonical {slug}-{id} rewrite preserves it. The input mirrors the committed query without overwriting a draft still being typed. A list read in flight keeps previous rows under the fetching indicator and a stale answer is discarded, so the screen never blanks.

nodes.label: serialize.ts Wire Shape
nodes.rationale: The shape of a GET response is fixed by serialize.ts emitting the wire types in packages/shared/src/types.ts, including the {seconds, nanoseconds} timestamp and media-proxy url fields.

nodes.label: Four Settings Tabs, Each Saving Its Own Half
nodes.norm_label: four settings tabs, each saving its own half
nodes.rationale: General, Public view, Access, Data are each an address (/settings/general …); a bare or unknown segment lands on General through the address rewrite, so an old settings link needs no redirect route. Each tab saves only its own half, which the pure decision beside the page answers; Save is off while the decision answers an empty payload. Inactive panels are not kept mounted, which is why the access card fetches nothing until reached.

nodes.label: One Lambda Serving API and SPA Behind One HTTP API
nodes.norm_label: one lambda serving api and spa behind one http api
nodes.rationale: Running API and built SPA in one Lambda gives a same-origin app with no CORS to configure; notably it also guarantees client and server ship together, so a partial-update protocol cannot skew between halves.

nodes.label: SkinHost Scoping and the No-Portaled-Component Rule
nodes.norm_label: skinhost scoping and the no-portaled-component rule
nodes.rationale: SkinHost scopes a skin's CSS variables so its type scale cannot leak onto /manage; a skin must not use a portaled Mantine component, which would render outside that scope. Skins register in registry.ts (basicx default) and stored options resolve against declared specs with an unknown key reported rather than silently dropped.

nodes.label: Soft Delete via deletedAt and the Deleted View
nodes.norm_label: soft delete via deletedat and the deleted view
nodes.rationale: The stamp removes the work from every live list while the bytes stay; the Deleted view lists stamped works most recently deleted first and restores one or many. Restore clears the stamp and touches nothing else. No purge and no retention window exist, so a deleted row lives until restored.

nodes.label: SPA Routes (public vs /manage)
nodes.rationale: Public: /, /login, /signup, /reset-password, /invite/:token (shows the collection and invited email before sign-in), and the skin-rendered /collection/:id and /collection/:id/artwork/:id. Protected: everything under /manage.

nodes.label: COLLECTION_LIMITS Shared by API and Client
nodes.norm_label: collection_limits shared by api and client
nodes.rationale: One map imported by both sides so the API's enforcement and the client's messaging cannot disagree; the API returns limit-reached (409) on create. The cap counts owned collections only — collaborations do not count, and a transfer may take the recipient over the cap without being refused.

nodes.label: Dev as a Full Disposable Replica of Production
nodes.norm_label: dev as a full disposable replica of production
nodes.rationale: Dev has its own database, bucket, certificate, AUTH_SECRET and Resend key so a wrecked dev database, wiped bucket or revoked mail key cannot touch production. Dev is public and noindexed, which lets the shipped client and the verify pass run against it unchanged; NODE_ENV=production on both because it is what makes the session cookie Secure.

nodes.label: Unlock Throttle: Fixed Window, Atomic Claim
nodes.norm_label: unlock throttle: fixed window, atomic claim
nodes.rationale: Ten failures spend a fixed ten-minute window floored from the attempt's own time; the eleventh is refused unread with 429 that states the window and never the time left (no Retry-After, for the same reason). The claim is one atomic ON CONFLICT … WHERE attempts < 10 upsert so two racing attempts cannot both pass. A right password clears the pair's counter rows. The address is the gateway's sourceIp passed in x-arcula-client-ip, overwriting client input, because a forwarding header is client-supplied. Identity is honest rather than complete: an address is shared behind a proxy and cheap to multiply, so this raises the cost of guessing without being a proof.

nodes.label: Photo Variant Geometry (xxlarge … square_sm)
nodes.rationale: xxlarge (max 3000, inside) is the Collection PDF's source because its photo box needs 2417 px at 300 dpi, past xlarge's 2400 cap, and it is the widest srcSet candidate. A document image gets only square_sm and large — the two a document actually renders with. A PDF has no variants; the original is the whole entry.

nodes.label: First-Run Provisioning Order
nodes.rationale: The order is forced because a host's d-… routing target does not exist until the stack has deployed once, and both environments share one account and bootstrap: bootstrap once → create the Postgres project and .env.<env> → provision the us-east-1 certificate → push dev and apply GitHub settings (Environments admitted only to their branch, two OIDC roles) → deploy once → publish the routing record and deploy again to finish and verify.

nodes.label: Arcula Design Record (project-plan.md)
nodes.rationale: As-built description of the product, data model and architecture; where doc and code disagree the code is right and the doc is a bug to fix.

nodes.label: The Not-Built List
nodes.rationale: Deliberately absent: a read-only collaborator role (needs a second permission matrix), per-work attribution and audit trail, transfer acceptance, rate limiting beyond the unlock throttle, a collaborator cap, account deletion, purge/retention for deleted works, collection deletion, export, search beyond the ten-field query, tiers/billing, and an always-on container (infra/Dockerfile is the documented scale-up path).

nodes.label: Access Is Membership (Inside vs Outside the Collection)
nodes.norm_label: access is membership (inside vs outside the collection)
nodes.rationale: The membership fact decides which matrix applies. Inside: owner and collaborators read every live work (drafts included), a deleted work by id, and documents at every status, and every write asks requireMemberCollection. Outside: the collection is the only gate and a Visitor equals an anonymous reader (membership null) — signing in buys nothing there.

nodes.label: The Collection Is the Only Visitor Gate
nodes.norm_label: the collection is the only visitor gate
nodes.rationale: A visitor sees a published, live work exactly when its collection is public; draft, deleted and private are one answer. A blocked work answers a uniform 404 because saying which was refused would be a disclosure; a private collection answers 403, which the client maps to its private state. A test pins the SQL list filter and the pure verdict to the same answer.

nodes.label: Design Bet: Art Is Not Tidy Data
nodes.norm_label: design bet: art is not tidy data
nodes.rationale: An unset field is not an empty one; acquisitionDate is free text ("circa 1889") not a date; money is stored as typed rather than parsed to a float. The whole schema is this bet made concrete.

nodes.label: Forward-Only Migrations and the Schema-Ships-Alone Rule
nodes.norm_label: forward-only migrations and the schema-ships-alone rule
nodes.rationale: deploy.sh deploys the Lambda before it migrates, so a release carrying both a new table and its code would serve requests against missing tables. A NOT NULL column ships nullable first and is tightened in the release that writes it, because one migration setting NOT NULL would break the old code's inserts. A revert therefore only redeploys code and leaves the schema.

nodes.label: Protected = the Gate Plus a Second Condition, Not a Third Visibility
nodes.norm_label: protected = the gate plus a second condition, not a third visibility
nodes.rationale: A password on a public collection is an extra condition in front of the visitor gate, so the verdict stays one predicate with the grant as a fact beside membership. Membership bypasses the challenge; the grant admits exactly what a visitor sees; a private collection stays closed to a grant holder. The anonymous list excludes protected collections like private ones: a protected collection is shared as a link, not found in an index. A refused read answers 403 password-required with the name — the deliberate contrast with the invitation token's uniform not-found, because here the artefact is not the secret.

nodes.label: Every Read Goes Through the API (One Authorization Layer)
nodes.norm_label: every read goes through the api (one authorization layer)
nodes.rationale: Rows and bytes both pass through the API so one authorization layer covers row and object alike; media never streams straight from S3.

nodes.label: collectionPassword.ts
nodes.rationale: hashPassword (scrypt with cost encoded in the string) and verifyPassword; no plaintext is stored or logged and a malformed hash is a failed check, not a 500.

nodes.label: unlockThrottle.ts
nodes.rationale: Holds only the throttle's policy — the fixed ten-minute window and the flooring that names the span an attempt belongs to.

nodes.label: x-arcula-client-ip Address
nodes.rationale: The throttle's address is the gateway's sourceIp written by the Lambda entry, never read from a client-supplied forwarding header, so a client cannot choose the bucket it is counted in.

nodes.label: Password Write on PATCH /collections/:id
nodes.rationale: password has three meanings — a string sets it (eight characters minimum, deliberately not trimmed), null removes it, an absent key leaves the column alone (so public→private→public returns to Protected). Plaintext is scrypt-hashed with cost parameters encoded in the stored string before the transaction; the settings write and the deletion of every Access grant row commit together so a password change never leaves a reader holding a grant to the old password. The hash is never a wire field.

nodes.label: POST /collections/:id/unlock
nodes.rationale: Accepts any non-empty guess (a short guess is a wrong password, not a malformed request). Right password → 201 {unlocked:true} plus the grant cookie; wrong → 403 invalid-password, deliberately distinct from an invitation token's uniform not-found because the lock screen already named the collection; no password or a Private collection → 409; unknown → 404. A grant admits exactly what a visitor sees.

nodes.label: Unlock Throttle
nodes.rationale: Counted in collection_unlock_attempts per address, collection and fixed ten-minute window floored from the attempt's own time; ten failures spend the window and the eleventh is refused unread as 429 too-many-attempts. The refusal states the window not the time left and sends no Retry-After; a right password deletes the counter rows so a mistyping member carries no debt; keying on the pair stops one collection's throttle locking a shared address out of another's.

nodes.label: collection_unlock_attempts Table
nodes.rationale: Written and read by the unlock route alone, which is the throttle's whole surface.

nodes.label: collectionLimitForTier / COLLECTION_LIMITS
nodes.rationale: The quota counts owned collections only; a collaboration does not consume it.

nodes.label: Better Auth Core Tables
nodes.rationale: user, session, account and verification, with user extended by the four typed custom columns firstName, lastName, tier and settings that the API declares to the adapter.

nodes.label: Partial Unique Pending-Invitation Index
nodes.rationale: collection_invitations stores the token's hash, never the token, with one pending offer per collection and address enforced as a partial unique index.

nodes.label: Runtime-Free Schema
nodes.rationale: No driver, no driver-specific types, no DOM: the package's tests read the migration off disk so Node types are available, and the DOM-free guarantee is the tsconfig lib array. @arcula/shared is the client-contract side of the same wall.

nodes.label: Schema as Single Source of Truth
nodes.norm_label: schema as single source of truth
nodes.rationale: src/index.ts is imported by the API over a live driver, read by drizzle-kit to generate migrations, and asserted by tests. A table added by hand outside the schema is still open because RLS defaults to off — one reason the schema stays the single source of truth.

nodes.label: One AWS Account, One CDK Bootstrap (ADR-0002)
nodes.norm_label: one aws account, one cdk bootstrap (adr-0002)
nodes.rationale: The two environments share one AWS account and one CDK bootstrap, so a modified dev workflow could reach production's stack — but cannot read production's secrets. The limits of the isolation are real and recorded rather than assumed away.

nodes.label: scripts/deploy.sh (the one deploy sequence)
nodes.rationale: cdk build → cdk deploy → resolve the URL → migrate → seed → re-deploy with the real PUBLIC_URL → deploy-verify. deploy-prod.sh and deploy-dev.sh are thin wrappers and CI calls the same scripts, so the sequence has exactly one definition. The Lambda deploy precedes the migrate step, which is why schema changes ship alone.

nodes.label: dev Environment (dev.arcula.art)
nodes.rationale: Dev is public, noindexed and disposable, with its own database, bucket, certificate, AUTH_SECRET and Resend key; its /api/health reports the deployed commit, which production's does not.

nodes.label: infra/cdk (the CDK stack, not a workspace member)
nodes.norm_label: infra/cdk (the cdk stack, not a workspace member)
nodes.rationale: It installs its own dependencies, so cd infra/cdk && bun install must run once before bun run check can resolve aws-cdk-lib.

nodes.label: Merging Is Deploying
nodes.rationale: check.yml runs the gate on PRs; deploy-dev.yml and deploy-prod.yml run the gate again on push then build and deploy through scripts/deploy.sh — the same script a laptop runs, so the sequence has one definition. Dev cancels a superseded run; production never cancels, so two migrations cannot interleave against the production database.

nodes.label: Migrations Are Forward-Only
nodes.rationale: packages/db/migrations/ is generated and applied, never reversed, so reverting a commit redeploys the code but leaves the schema where it was. A revert is safe only when the release's change was additive; a revert of a destructive migration leaves old code against a schema that no longer matches it and needs a compensating migration written by hand.

nodes.label: Rule: Never Commit a Secret
nodes.rationale: The repository is public, so this is not a style preference. Per-environment values live in infra/cdk/.env.<env> (gitignored) and in GitHub Environments; SEED_*, DATABASE_URL, AUTH_SECRET, RESEND_API_KEY and CERT_ARN are secrets or variables there, never in the tree.

nodes.label: Rule: Never Use the Fork-Exposing pull_request_target Event
nodes.norm_label: rule: never use the fork-exposing pull_request_target event
nodes.rationale: pull_request_target runs with the repository's secrets and hands them to a fork's code. A workflow that runs on a PR uses the plain pull_request event; check.yml is the model because it reads the PR's code and needs no secret at all.

nodes.label: A Schema Change Ships Alone
nodes.rationale: scripts/deploy.sh deploys the Lambda before it migrates, so a release carrying both a new table and the code that reads it would serve requests against a schema that is not there yet. Additive changes are safe in the intermediate release because old code ignores them; a column that must end NOT NULL is added nullable in that release and tightened in the release that writes it.

nodes.label: Apex and www Are Separate DomainName Pairs
nodes.norm_label: apex and www are separate domainname pairs
nodes.rationale: An HTTP-API custom domain serves only its exact host, so pointing www at the apex target is the 403 the layout is built to avoid. The stack emits both (ApiRegionalDomainName, ApiRegionalDomainNameForwww), each with its own regional endpoint, and the apex and www targets are different d-… values.

nodes.label: 0003_shared_collections + 0004_media_namespace_not_null
nodes.rationale: The schema shipped in two releases: 0003 created the sharing tables and added mediaNamespaceId nullable backfilled from userId, the feature code read mediaNamespaceId ?? userId through the gap, and 0004 backfilled only the rows the old code wrote in between (WHERE mediaNamespaceId IS NULL) and set the column NOT NULL. This is the worked example of the forward-only rule.

nodes.label: The Three Hand Edits to Generated Migrations
nodes.norm_label: the three hand edits to generated migrations
nodes.rationale: Hand edits are deliberately few: a data backfill appended to the generated file, the add-nullable → backfill → set-not-null sequence for a column that cannot be added NOT NULL on an existing table, and a grant revoke drizzle-kit cannot model — it renders schema, never grants, so 0006_enable_rls appends its guarded block by hand.

nodes.label: Access Grant
nodes.rationale: A 32-byte token in the cookie named for its collection (arcula_grant_{id}, Path=/api/v1, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, twelve hours); the row stores only its SHA-256 hash with the same expiry. The cookie path is broad because the media proxy is one route for every collection's bytes, so the name is the scope and a grant minted elsewhere is never consulted. A grant admits exactly what a visitor sees — published live works, never a draft, never a document — and a private collection stays shut to a grant holder.

nodes.label: collectionGrants.ts (grant facts)
nodes.rationale: Pure facts — mintGrantToken, hashGrantToken, grantCookieName, isGrantUsable — with GRANT_TTL_MS (twelve hours) the one number behind both the cookie's Max-Age and the row's expiry. No database and no Hono: the unlock route mints and stores, the read paths load the row and ask this.

nodes.label: Lock Screen (app chrome, not a skin)
nodes.norm_label: lock screen (app chrome, not a skin)
nodes.rationale: A refused collection read is 403 password-required with details.collectionName, which the public pages fold to the lock screen; success calls the hook's reload to re-run the ordinary load, collection read first, and an expired grant lands back on the lock screen the same way.

nodes.label: Protected Collection (a second condition, not a third state)
nodes.norm_label: protected collection (a second condition, not a third state)
nodes.rationale: A password is a second condition on a public collection, never a third visibility state (ADR-0005). collections.passwordHash nullable is the whole stored protection; the member read carries isPasswordProtected derived from the hash's presence and the hash never leaves the server. Membership bypasses the challenge; a visitor needs an Access grant.

nodes.label: A Skin Must Not Use a Portaled Mantine Component
nodes.norm_label: a skin must not use a portaled mantine component
nodes.rationale: Modal, Drawer, Menu, Popover, Select, Combobox and Tooltip all render into document.body, outside the skin's scope, and would silently pick up the app theme.

nodes.label: POST /collections/:id/unlock
nodes.rationale: 201 and the cookie on success, 403 invalid-password on a wrong password, 409 on a collection with no password (or a private one, where there is nothing to get past), and 429 too-many-attempts once the window is spent.

nodes.label: Access Grant (glossary sense)
nodes.rationale: What a reader holds after entering a protected collection's password: scoped to one collection, expiring, verified on every request, and admitting the reader to the public view but not to the collection as a member.

nodes.label: Artworks Manage View (Table or Grid)
nodes.rationale: A manage-page presentation only — Table for scanning recorded fields, Grid of photo cards for recognising works by their images — never how a visitor sees the collection, which is a skin's business.

nodes.label: Lock Screen
nodes.rationale: App chrome, never a skin, because the lock belongs to the collection rather than to how the collection is presented; the public views call the state it puts them in 'locked' and a refused read is what reaches it.

nodes.label: Protected
nodes.rationale: A public collection that also requires its password — a second condition on public readability rather than a visibility of its own. It is absent from the public list and reachable only by its link, and the owner and collaborators never face the challenge.

nodes.label: Skin
nodes.rationale: The presentation a public collection is rendered in — its type, layout and chrome — and never how a visitor is admitted, which belongs to the collection.

nodes.label: Collection Invitation
nodes.rationale: One pending row per collection and lowercased email, the SHA-256 hash of a single-use token, a seven-day expiry and a status; the raw token exists only in the mail. Acceptance needs the mailed token and a session whose email matches the invited address; the invitee's GET /me/invitations lists live offers and can decline one, because acceptance is the mail's job.

nodes.label: invitations.ts (token algebra and row questions)
nodes.rationale: isInvitationUsable is pending and not past expiresAt; isInvitationResendable is pending and the last issue older than the 60-second cooldown — expiry is deliberately not part of it.

nodes.label: Media Namespace (mediaNamespaceId)
nodes.rationale: Final object keys use the collection's mediaNamespaceId, fixed at creation, so a transfer changes the owner and the artwork mirror and moves no object: existing URLs keep working. Staging keys use the uploader's id, so one collaborator's unsaved upload is never under another's prefix.

nodes.label: Two Mails, Best Effort
nodes.rationale: Sharing adds exactly two mails: the invitation (linking to CLIENT_ORIGIN/invite/:token) and the ownership-transfer notice. The invitation row is written before the mail is attempted, so a provider failure answers emailSent: false and the owner can resend after the 60-second cooldown; a transfer commits before its notice, so a failed notice never undoes the transfer.

nodes.label: Account Mail
nodes.rationale: Mail about an account's own security or identity — password reset, address verification — sent because the account asked for it or needs it, and never suppressed by an email preference.

nodes.label: Invitation
nodes.rationale: A pending offer to become a collaborator, addressed to an email, carried by a single-use token, expiring after seven days; accepting one is how an invited account becomes a collaborator.

nodes.label: Ownership Transfer
nodes.rationale: Moves a collection's owner to one of its collaborators; the previous owner stays as a collaborator, and only the owner may begin one.

nodes.label: Relationship Mail
nodes.rationale: A notice about an existing relationship between two parties rather than about the account itself: an invitation, or the notice that an ownership transfer has happened.

nodes.label: Reset Request
nodes.rationale: Answered with the same sentence whether or not an account exists, so the reset path does not disclose which addresses are registered.

nodes.label: Staged
nodes.rationale: An uploaded file held for an artwork still being edited and not yet part of the collection; distinct from a draft work.

nodes.label: Hono App (app.ts)
nodes.rationale: Owns the onError error envelope, the www-to-configured-origin 308 redirect, dev-origin CORS, GET /api/health, and the mounts (/api/auth, /api/v1, then the SPA).

nodes.label: responsePolicy.ts
nodes.rationale: Environment-derived response decisions as pure functions (canonical-host redirect, health body, noindex flag); env.ts reads the inputs once and the app hands them in, so no environment's hostname or commit is written into the source.

nodes.label: SPA Serving Middleware (spa.ts)
nodes.rationale: Serves index.html for every non-/api path (deep links included); index.html is never cached, hashed assets are immutable, and a missing dist tree leaves the middleware inert so Vite is the SPA in dev.

nodes.label: Bun and Lambda Entry Points
nodes.rationale: One app runs on Bun locally (Bun.serve on PORT 8000) and on a Node 24 Lambda in production; the lambda adapter carries Set-Cookie in the top-level cookies array (not multiValueHeaders) and base64-encodes binary bodies.

nodes.label: Uniform Error Envelope
nodes.rationale: All /api/v1 responses share one envelope so clients parse one shape; Better Auth's /api/auth/* is deliberately unwrapped because its response shape is what @better-auth/react consumes.

nodes.label: artwork_photo_variants (parentId, key) Upsert
nodes.rationale: Keying on (parentId, key) is what makes a re-save an idempotent upsert.

nodes.label: Single-Transaction Save with Accepted Residual
nodes.rationale: A save is one Postgres transaction (field write, staged-to-final S3 copy, row upserts, deletes for dropped entries). S3 copies cannot roll back with the rows, so a failed save may leave final objects with no row — an accepted residual that the staging lifecycle and the sweep route exist to clean up.

nodes.label: email/provider.ts
nodes.rationale: SMTP locally and Resend in production; a provider failure surfaces as emailSent:false rather than failing the write.

nodes.label: normalizeEmail
nodes.rationale: The one trim-and-lowercase an address gets on both sides of every comparison.

nodes.label: Invitation Loop
nodes.rationale: POST /collections/:id/invitations writes a pending row and mails CLIENT_ORIGIN/invite/:token; the raw token is never stored (only its SHA-256 hash) and acceptance needs both the token and a session whose email matches.

nodes.label: Ownership Transfer
nodes.rationale: Target must already be a collaborator; one transaction moves collections.userId, mirrors artworks.userId, removes the recipient's membership row and inserts the previous owner's. The fixed media namespace means no object moves and every existing URL keeps serving; the notice mail is sent after commit and emailSent:false never undoes the transfer.

nodes.label: Hosted Wordmark arcula-name-logo.png
nodes.rationale: The wordmark is apps/web/public/arcula-name-logo.png — the one the SPA serves, not a second copy — and it is the only image a mail carries.

nodes.label: collections.userId as the One Owner Fact
nodes.norm_label: collections.userid as the one owner fact
nodes.rationale: A collaborator is a row in collection_collaborators and the owner is not duplicated there; artworks.userId is a mirror of the collection owner, not an authorization fact.

nodes.label: Dev Reply-To Left Empty on Purpose
nodes.norm_label: dev reply-to left empty on purpose
nodes.rationale: Dev has no monitored inbox and the code never invents an address; the invitation footer offers a reply only when a Reply-To is configured and otherwise says the mail can be ignored, so it never promises a person behind an unmonitored address.

nodes.label: DMARC Reporting Then Enforcement
nodes.rationale: The record currently is v=DMARC1; p=none with no reporting, so there is no evidence of what fails and nothing stops forgery. The staged path is p=none with rua → p=quarantine → p=reject over weeks. Dev gets its own _dmarc.dev.arcula.art at p=none so production's enforcement never catches dev. Do not add ruf and do not rely on pct (poorly supported). This is a DNS change on reports, not a release, so never bundle it with a deploy.

nodes.label: One Mail Identity
nodes.rationale: Four mails are composed by one module with one identity: Arcula <noreply@arcula.art> as sender, Arcula <hello@arcula.art> as Reply-To when EMAIL_REPLY_TO is set, the hosted wordmark, one call-to-action with the same URL in the text part, a line saying why the message arrived, and no tracking pixel.

nodes.label: Email Opt-Out Deferred Until Complaints
nodes.rationale: The four mails are two account mails and two relationship notices, which Resend's guidance treats as exempt, so no opt-out ships and no mail promises one; revisit if deliverability insights show complaints. The shape when built: an email_opt_outs table keyed by normalised address, an HMAC token, RFC 8058 one-click GET/POST, List-Unsubscribe headers on invitation mail only, invitation create and resend refusing a suppressed address, account mail and the transfer notice never suppressed so an account can always recover, and the migration shipping in its own release.

nodes.label: media/keys.ts Object-Key Algebra
nodes.rationale: The key parser is what makes the media proxy's per-request authorization work from the key alone; with sharing, final keys use the collection's fixed mediaNamespaceId and staging keys use the uploader's id.

nodes.label: 0003_shared_collections Migration
nodes.rationale: Creates the two sharing tables, replaces the owner-list index and adds mediaNamespaceId nullable backfilled from userId; it shipped alone, the feature code followed, and 0004 tightened the column afterwards.

nodes.label: 0004_media_namespace_not_null Migration
nodes.rationale: Backfills only the rows the old code wrote in between (WHERE mediaNamespaceId IS NULL, so a namespace the new code minted survives) and then sets the column NOT NULL.

nodes.label: 0006_enable_rls Migration
nodes.rationale: enableRLS() makes drizzle-kit generate the thirteen ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY statements, but a grant lives in Postgres's ACL and not in the schema declaration, so the guarded DO block revoking anon and authenticated is appended by hand. The guard is deliberate: Supabase creates those roles while the local stack and CI have neither, so an unguarded REVOKE FROM anon would fail every db:migrate with role "anon" does not exist.

nodes.label: collections.mediaNamespaceId
nodes.rationale: Fixed at creation, so an ownership transfer moves no object and existing URLs keep working.

nodes.label: Structural Contract Tests
nodes.rationale: Assert the in-memory schema and the committed migration against each other's ground truth — table shapes, CHECKs, the artwork-list indexes, the collaborator userId index, the partial unique pending-invitation index, the nullable → backfill → NOT NULL order, timestamptz, defaults, and the lock-down (RLS on all thirteen tables plus the guarded revoke and the absence of FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY).

nodes.label: Add-Nullable → Backfill → Set-Not-Null
nodes.rationale: A column that cannot be added NOT NULL on an existing table is added nullable, backfilled, and tightened afterwards, split across releases so old code stays valid in between.

nodes.label: Forward-Only Migrations
nodes.rationale: Gerated SQL is committed and applied, never reversed; hand edits are limited to three documented cases (a data backfill appended after generation, because drizzle-kit renders schema and never data; the add-nullable → backfill → set-not-null sequence; and a grant revoke drizzle-kit cannot model). Nothing else is edited by hand.

nodes.label: RLS Lock-down with Zero Policies
nodes.rationale: Every table enables RLS with zero policies so the PostgREST roles see nothing; the API connects as the table owner, which bypasses RLS, so the lock-down is invisible to the product. FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY must never be added, because it would subject the owner to the empty policy set and blank every read.

nodes.label: Accepted supabase_admin Default-ACL Residue (#181)
nodes.rationale: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES is per-grantor: 0006 runs as postgres, which is not a member of supabase_admin, so the platform's second book of defaults survives and supabase_admin keeps full grants for both client roles on tables and sequences it creates. The residue is accepted because every table in the schema is created by drizzle-kit migrate as postgres, so the product's own path starts closed, and the surviving grants become reachable only with the Data API enabled and a table created in public by supabase_admin outside the schema. Closing it would be dashboard state, not repository state.

nodes.label: Sharing Is Membership
nodes.rationale: collections.userId is the one owner fact and collection_collaborators holds everyone else; the owner is not duplicated there, and a membership row is the authorization fact for everything inside the collection. Accepted in ADR-0004.

nodes.label: Collaborator
nodes.rationale: Records and edits artworks and changes the collection's settings, including whether it is public, but may not invite, remove or transfer.

nodes.label: Owner
nodes.rationale: The only party who may invite, remove or transfer, and the account the tier cap counts; an artwork's owner is its collection's owner.

nodes.label: Private
nodes.rationale: Readable by its owner and collaborators alone; to a visitor a private collection is indistinguishable from one that does not exist.

nodes.label: Public
nodes.rationale: Readable by a visitor. Only a collection carries this choice: it is the gate on everything inside it, and a work is never public on its own account.

nodes.label: Shared (vs Public)
nodes.rationale: A collection whose owner has added collaborators, which is distinct from Public (readable by visitors); neither implies the other.

nodes.label: Tier
nodes.rationale: The allowance an account is on and the unit the collection cap counts against; the cap counts the collections an account owns, not those shared with it.

nodes.label: Pure Access Verdicts (access.ts)
nodes.rationale: Pure functions over the collection, the viewer's membership and the row, so the authorization truth can be reasoned about and tested without HTTP or database.

nodes.label: artworkRead.ts
nodes.rationale: The single read path for works, one and listed, with the access verdict applied over the rows it loads; it carries no HTTP type because the route owns the wire codes.

nodes.label: Membership Loading (authorize.ts)
nodes.rationale: Loads the collection and the viewer's membership row for every read; every write path asks the same membership question via requireMemberCollection / requireMemberArtwork so non-members get 403 and missing collections 404.

nodes.label: Access Ending: Removal and Leaving
nodes.rationale: Both delete the membership row so the account is a visitor on the next request and discard that account's staging prefix best effort — a storage failure does not fail the action, since the staging lifecycle is the backstop; saved works and final objects are untouched.

nodes.label: 403 password-required Challenge
nodes.rationale: A refused collection read is 403 password-required with details.collectionName so the public pages can fold to the lock screen; a refused work list is 403 forbidden and a single work or photo object is 404, because only the collection read is the challenge.

nodes.rationale: Output that contradicts an existing ADR surfaces it rather than silently overriding it.
